metaData.title: Sunbelt Literacy Network autumn appeal review

sentences.text: Afternoon. The autumn appeal goes out next week, so I wanted to catch you before rather than after.
Afternoon, and I appreciate that. After is when I have opinions and before is when they are useful.
How large is the send this year?
Just under nine thousand households, which is about a thousand more than last autumn.
We are asking for a little less per household and hoping more of them say yes, which is the advice we were given.
That is the advice I would have given too. How did the spring send perform?
Poorly, and we know why now, which is the only good thing about it.
Our appeal letters are landing in junk for anyone on the two large free mail providers, and we only learned that because a board member mentioned it in passing.
He asked why we had stopped writing to him, and we had written to him four times.
When we went looking, roughly a third of the list was in the same position, and that third gave almost nothing in the spring.
A third of the list is a serious share. Did you get any figures on how it varied by provider?
The two big consumer providers were the worst by a distance. Anyone on a work address seemed to receive it normally.
We have no way of seeing that from inside the system, so all of this came from telephoning forty donors and asking them to check.
Forty telephone calls to diagnose a mail problem is not a reasonable thing to have had to do.
I will put the spring figures and this week's list size into the write up together.
If it helps, I kept the notes from all forty calls and they are fairly consistent.
Send them over and I will attach them. Was there anything else on your side?
One thing that is nothing to do with the appeal, and it comes from our operations manager rather than me.
Our staff keep a separate password for this system and nothing else, and we want them signing in with the same account they use for everything else in the office.
We have twenty six staff and four of them lock themselves out in any given month, which lands on her desk.
It is a small thing that happens often, which in my experience is the most annoying kind of thing.
That is a clear enough ask and it is one I hear from organisations of your size fairly often.
Let me take it back with the same words you have just used rather than my own shorthand for it.
Please take it back in her words. She will be pleased I remembered to mention it, which is not something that happens every week.
Two items then, the mail problem with the spring figures and the sign in request from your operations manager.
I will have both written up before the appeal goes out next week.
That is all I wanted. Good luck to all of us on Tuesday.
